title: Green System Engine Driven Pump — Installation
abstract: Installation of the green system engine driven pump on the accessory gearbox, with the spline lubrication, the fill and bleed sequence and the leak check at operating pressure that closes the task.

sections.purpose: This task installs the green system engine driven pump on the accessory gearbox pad, fills and bleeds the circuit, and proves the installation at operating pressure.
sections.job_setup_note: Do this task with the green system depressurised and the reservoir still locked out. The drive spline must be lubricated with the correct grease and not with hydraulic fluid; the wrong lubricant is the most common cause of an early repeat failure. Filling and bleeding cannot be rushed because air trapped in the case drain leg will show as a soft pedal on the first cycle. Two persons are needed at the pylon.
sections.procedure: 1. Check the gearbox pad seal face and fit a new pad seal. 2. Lubricate the drive spline with the specified grease. CAUTION: DO NOT LUBRICATE THE SPLINE WITH HYDRAULIC FLUID. THE SPLINE WILL WEAR AND THE PUMP WILL FAIL EARLY. 3. Offer the pump to the pad, keeping the drive shaft square until the spline engages. 4. Install the gearbox mounting nuts and torque them in the sequence in the torque table. 5. Connect the pressure, suction and case drain lines, taking the caps off one at a time. 6. Install the inboard pipe FJO107150-27 and support it with the loop clamps AGS207234-50 at the marked positions. 7. Connect the left-hand depressurisation solenoid BE759984-33 and check its detent by hand. 8. Restore the reservoir and fill the green system to the correct level. 9. Bleed the circuit at the highest point and then at the case drain leg. WARNING: DO NOT PRESSURISE THE SYSTEM UNTIL EVERY CAP IS OFF AND EVERY JOINT IS MADE. 10. Pressurise the green system and do a leak check at every disturbed joint at operating pressure. 11. Check the right-hand actuator DU841059-74 for correct operation through one full cycle.
sections.close_out: Close the pylon fairings. Record the installation, the pump serial number, the torque values and the bleed result in the aircraft technical log. Confirm the fluid level after the system has been cycled and settled.

safety_precautions: Do not pressurise the system until every cap is off and every joint is made.
Wear eye protection and gloves rated for phosphate ester fluid.
Keep clear of the accessory gearbox during the first pressurisation.

title: Green System Engine Driven Pump — Installation

issue.reason: Case drain filter installation and servicing are added at step 5 and the differential pressure indicator check with its bypass threshold at step 12.

abstract: Installation of the green system engine driven pump on the accessory gearbox, with the spline lubrication, the fill and bleed sequence and the differential pressure indicator check that closes the task on modified aircraft.

sections.purpose: This task installs the green system engine driven pump on the accessory gearbox pad, fills and bleeds the circuit, and proves the installation at operating pressure.
sections.job_setup_note: Do this task with the green system depressurised and the reservoir still locked out. The drive spline must be lubricated with the correct grease and not with hydraulic fluid; the wrong lubricant is the most common cause of an early repeat failure. Filling and bleeding cannot be rushed because air trapped in the case drain leg will show as a false differential pressure reading. Two persons are needed at the pylon. Access note: the pump is reached through the pylon aft fairing, which is the same opening the aft fairing heat shield work uses, so where both are due in the same check, plan them into one opening.
sections.procedure: 1. Check the gearbox pad seal face and fit a new pad seal. 2. Lubricate the drive spline with the specified grease. CAUTION: DO NOT LUBRICATE THE SPLINE WITH HYDRAULIC FLUID. THE SPLINE WILL WEAR AND THE PUMP WILL FAIL EARLY. 3. Offer the pump to the pad, keeping the drive shaft square until the spline engages. 4. Install the gearbox mounting nuts and torque them in the sequence in the torque table. 5. Where the case drain filter is fitted, service it before the lines are connected: fit a new element unless the element in the bowl has less than 500 flight hours, fill the bowl with clean fluid, install the bowl on its bracket and connect the pump side first so that the element is not run dry at the first pressurisation. 6. Connect the pressure, suction and case drain lines, taking the caps off one at a time. 7. Install the inboard pipe FJO107150-27 and support it with the loop clamps AGS207234-50 at the marked positions. 8. Connect the left-hand depressurisation solenoid BE759984-33 and check its detent by hand. 9. Restore the reservoir and fill the green system to the correct level. 10. Bleed the circuit at the highest point and then at the case drain leg. WARNING: DO NOT PRESSURISE THE SYSTEM UNTIL EVERY CAP IS OFF AND EVERY JOINT IS MADE. 11. Pressurise the green system and do a leak check at every disturbed joint at operating pressure. 12. On modified aircraft, check the differential pressure indicator with the system at operating pressure and the fluid above 25 degrees Celsius. The indicator is clear below 2.4 bar across the element and pops at 3.4 bar, which is the bypass threshold; a reading between the two is not visible on the indicator, so where the element has been in service and the indicator is clear, still record the element hours. CAUTION: DO NOT RESET A POPPED INDICATOR AND RETURN THE AIRCRAFT TO SERVICE. A POPPED INDICATOR MEANS THE ELEMENT HAS REACHED BYPASS AND THE CIRCUIT HAS SEEN UNFILTERED FLOW. 13. Check the right-hand actuator DU841059-74 for correct operation through one full cycle.
sections.close_out: Close the pylon fairings. Record the installation, the pump serial number, the torque values, the bleed result and the differential pressure indicator state in the aircraft technical log. Where a filter element was fitted, record its part number and the aircraft hours at fitment; the element is a life item and the operator maintenance programme tracks it. Confirm the fluid level after the system has been cycled and settled.

type_data.effectivity_note: All SOLANO-30 and SOLANO-34 aircraft; steps 5 and 12 apply to aircraft post MOD-131570 only

safety_precautions: Do not pressurise the system until every cap is off and every joint is made.
Wear eye protection and gloves rated for phosphate ester fluid.
Do not reset a tripped differential pressure indicator before the reading is recorded.
